title: Pilot Study to Evaluate Safety and Efficacy of PolyCore, a Ternary Combination of Xylitol, L-Carnitine and Polydextrin, to Treat End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients Starting Peritoneal Dialysis (EXCITE)
official: Pilot Study to Evaluate Safety and Efficacy of PolyCore, a Ternary Combination of Xylitol, L-Carnitine and Polydextrin, to Treat End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients Starting Peritoneal Dialysis (EXCITE)
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to evaluate the safety of PolyCore through continuous monitoring of adverse events, vital signs, and laboratory parameters.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults with End-Stage Kidney Disease
2. GFR ≥ 5
3. Patients in treatment with peritoneal dialysis for less than 6 months (at screening visit) and in stable clinical conditions
4. Patients in incremental PD treatment with 1 daily Icodextrin(7.5%)-based solution and 1 daily glucose (up to 1.5%)-based solution, according the IPD regimens allowed by the study (at screening and baseline visits)
5. Understand the nature and characteristics of the study and give informed consent to participate
6. Weekly Kt/V urea ≥ 1.7
Exclusion criteria:
1. Episode of peritonitis in the last 3 months
2. Hypersensitivity to any of the components of the study IMPs
3. History of primary hyperoxaluria or identification by genetic testing of a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant associated with primary hyperoxaluria
4. Patients with acute renal failure
5. Presence of contraindications to the use of Polydextrin-based peritoneal dialysis solutions: allergy to starch-based polymers, maltose or isomaltose intolerance, glycogen storage disease, pre-existing severe lactic acidosis
6. Patients with loss of peritoneal function or extensive adhesions compromising peritoneal function
7. patients with a history of abdominal surgery in the month preceding commencement of therapy, patients with abdominal fistulae, tumors, open wounds, herniae or other conditions which compromise the integrity of the abdominal wall, abdominal surface or intra-abdominal cavit
8. Uncorrectable mechanical defects that prevent effective PD or increase the risk of infection.
9. History of oxalate or lactate abnormalities considered clinically significant by the investigator
10. History or evidence of any other medical, neurological, or psychological condition that, in the clinical judgment of the investigator, would place the subject at undue risk of a significant AE or interfere with study assessments during the course of the tri
11. Enrolled in a clinical trial with an investigational product within 1 month before the start of the study
12. Suspected or history of drug and/or alcohol abuse
13. Severe pulmonary, cardiac, or hepatic disease/insufficiency
14. Clinically significant abnormal liver function tests (Gamma-GT and/or AST and/or ALT > 2 UNL; and/or total bilirubin > 3 UNL)
15. Any type of active malignancy. Patients with excised basal cell carcinoma of the skin may be included
16. Female patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding, or women of childbearing potential who are not using or are refusing to use an adequate contraceptive program
